text:
### Observed differences

- The balance between two alternative routes flipped. In the earlier window, about 46 in 100 traces contained A01, while about 54 in 100 contained A10 and A11; in the later window, about 52–53 in 100 contained A01 and about 47–48 in 100 contained A10 and A11 — a shift of roughly 6–7 cases per 100 in each direction [OCC001, OCC008, OCC009].
- The two routes remained strict alternatives in both windows: A01 never occurs in the same trace as A10 or A11 (co-occurrence 0 before and after), while A10 and A11 still always occur together, in both orders (A10 first in about 24 in 100 traces, A11 first in about 30 in 100 earlier and 24 in 100 later) and directly adjacent in about 95 in 100 of their shared traces [REL009, REL010, REL055, LAG030, LAG039].
- Both routes sit between A05 and A07, which appear in every trace in both windows. A05 precedes A01 in essentially all traces containing both (A05 before A01 rose from 39 to 49 in 100 traces as A01 became more frequent), and A01 is directly followed by A07 in about 95 in 100 of its occurrences in both windows; of A05's outgoing transitions, the share leading to A01 rose from about 39% to 49%, while the shares leading to A10 and A11 fell to about 21% and 23% [REL004, REL006, LAG006, DIR001, DIR002].
- Consistent with this mix shift, A07's typical position moved slightly earlier (median from 0.75 to about 0.67 of the sequence) and A10's median position moved from 0.5 to 0.25; these are event-position redistributions and do not by themselves show that activities were moved [POS003, POS004].
- Two smaller participation changes: A02 appeared in about 9 in 100 later traces versus about 5 in 100 earlier (18 vs 9 of 200 traces), always after A05 and after A07; A06 appeared in about 9–10 in 100 versus about 15 in 100 (19 vs 29 traces), still always preceded by A05. A03 and A04 shifted only by about 2–3 in 100 traces with low empirical strength, within the range of random sampling [OCC002, OCC005, REL013, REL015, REL035, LAG008, OCC003, OCC004].

### Inference

Support level: Weak hypothesis

The evidence suggests that the share of traces routed through A01 between A05 and A07 increased, while the share routed through the adjacent pair A10 and A11 decreased — from roughly 46/54 per 100 traces to roughly 52–53/47–48. The change is shown directly and consistently: the participation of A01, A10 and A11 moved by mirrored amounts; A01 and A10/A11 were mutually exclusive before and after, so existing alternative paths changed only in how often they are taken; A05's outgoing transitions shifted toward A01 and away from A10/A11; A10–A11 co-occurrence fell in step; and A07's position distribution moved earlier, as expected when fewer traces take the A10/A11 route [OCC001, OCC008, OCC009, REL004, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL055, DIR002, POS003].

What is missing is the ability to rule out sampling variation: the evidence carries no screening expectation, and the core items' empirical strengths of roughly 0.73–0.92 mean that random re-splits of unchanged data produce differences at least this large in about 1 in 12 to 1 in 4 comparisons. Because the whole pattern could be produced by a single fluctuation in one roughly 50/50 routing share between two 200-trace samples, that competing explanation remains open; the secondary A02 and A06 changes additionally rest on only 9–29 traces per window [OCC001, OCC008, OCC009, REL009, OCC002, OCC005].

Other differences: A02's participation doubled (about 5 to about 9 in 100 traces), appearing after A05 and after A07; A06's participation fell (about 15 to about 9–10 in 100 traces), still always preceded by A05 [OCC002, OCC005, REL013, REL015, REL035, LAG008].
